chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from some of his companions, who raised it (marfū'), saying:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Discuss among yourselves, meet one another, and narrate hadith; for indeed hadith is a polishing for the hearts. The hearts rust just as swords rust, and their polishing is hadith.'

key_terms.تَذَاكَرُوا: Mutual discussion/reminder — the reciprocal form emphasizes communal exchange, not solitary study
key_terms.جِلَاء: Polishing/cleansing — from the root j-l-w, to make something shine by removing dross; used for polishing metals
key_terms.رَفَعَهُ: Raised it (mursal) — a technical hadith term indicating the chain was elevated to the Prophet without specifying the full chain of transmission
key_terms.لَتَرِينُ: To rust/tarnish — from the root r-y-n (ران على القلب), used in the Quran (83:14) for the spiritual covering that forms on hearts due to sins

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the polishing of hearts through hadith?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) commands his community to engage in scholarly discussion, mutual visitation, and transmission of his teachings. He uses the striking metaphor of sword-polishing to explain that the heart, like iron, is susceptible to spiritual rust — negligence, heedlessness, and sin — and that the remedy is active engagement with hadith. This narration, transmitted through al-Hajjal with a mursal (raised) chain, reflects the early Islamic community's understanding that hadith transmission was not merely scholarship but a form of spiritual purification.
